# La Ruche — Agent Instructions (docs/)

Domain rules for `docs/`, mirrored from `.claude/rules/` (source of truth). Closer `AGENTS.md` files take priority over the repo-root one.

## Rule: doc-architecture

_Rules for modifying docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and related ADR files._

# Architecture Docs Rules

Source of truth: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. References: ADR-001 to ADR-012.

## When to modify

Only modify if change is **proven in code**: new migration, new `src/` module, stack change, or ADR created/amended. Never anticipate — use "planned" marker if needed.

## Mandatory

- New table / handler / `domain/` module / frontend store → update `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` same commit.
- Table/column/Rust type names → English identifiers from code only.
- "Planned, not yet implemented" entities → must reference an ADR or Epic. Do not code them without one.
- Schéma DB invariants are contracts — any change requires sync update here.
- Never delete an invariant without verifying it's no longer enforced in code.
- No external references (ADR, DDR, ticket numbers) in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` body — refs only.

## Do not put here

Product rules → `docs/PRD.md`. UX/tokens → `docs/DESIGN.md`. Legal obligations → `docs/LEGAL.md`.

## Rule: doc-design

_Rules for modifying docs/DESIGN.md, DDR files, and frontend component catalogue._

# Design System Docs Rules

Source of truth: `docs/DESIGN.md`. References: DDR-001 to DDR-006.

## When to modify

Only after a new DDR is validated. Edits: inline, minimal, in existing section. No new section without user approval.

## Mandatory

- No raw values (`px`, `hex`, `rem`) in `class`/`style` if a CSS token exists.
- New `atom`/`molecule`/`organism` → add to catalogue (`docs/DESIGN.md §2`) before use.
- Interactive primitives → wrap in `C*` component. Never import `radix-vue` directly in a feature view.
- `.tone--*` classes are pure CSS utilities — never redefine locally.
- No `<style>` block in feature views — use Tailwind utilities or catalogue components.
- `CFormFeedback` → always in `#footer` slot of `CModal`, never in body.
- No external references (ADR, ticket numbers) in `docs/DESIGN.md` body — DDR refs only.

## Do not put here

Backend/DB rules → `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Legal → `docs/LEGAL.md`. Product workflows → `docs/PRD.md`.

## Rule: doc-epics

_Rules for modifying docs/EPICS.md._

# Epics & Stories Rules

Source of truth for backlog: `docs/EPICS.md`. Legal coverage table: `docs/LEGAL.md` only.

## Lifecycle

`new`🆕 → `in progress` ⏳ → `delivered` ✅ (backend + frontend on real API) | `canceled ❌` → `out of scope` ❌ (moved to "Fonctionnalités hors scope" with justification).

## When to modify

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| Work started on a story | Add `⏳` |
| Story delivered (backend + frontend on real API) | Add `✅`, update epic status, update "État code actuel" |
| New story from PRD, ADR or legal obligation | Add story with explicit ref (`LEGAL.md §X.Y` / `PRD US-XX` / `ADR-XXX`) and reopen the epic if necessary |
| New epic decided | Add with status, PRD/ADR/DDR ref, and at least one story |
| Story out of scope | Move to "Fonctionnalités hors scope" with justification |
| New or amended legal reference in `LEGAL.md` | Create or update the linked story pointing to `LEGAL.md §X.Y` |

## Mandatory

- Never mark `✅` unless backend + frontend are both on the real API.
- Never include implementation details in a story (no filenames, DB schemas, function names, endpoints) — those belong in ADRs and code.
- Every story must reference a PRD, ADR, or `LEGAL.md §X.Y`.
- Never change an epic status without checking each of its stories.
- Never recreate a legal coverage table here — that lives exclusively in `docs/LEGAL.md`.

## Story format

```
* `EP-XXX-SYY` [✅] — Action verb + functional scope (LEGAL.md §X.Y)
```

## Cross-sync on delivery

When a `✅` story covers a legal obligation → update `docs/LEGAL.md` coverage (⚠️/❌ → ✅) in the same pass. Never anticipate: coverage ✅ only after effective delivery.

## Do not put here

Implementation details → ADRs and code. Legal coverage table → `docs/LEGAL.md`. Feature detail → `docs/product/PRD - *.md`.

## Rule: doc-legal

_Rules for modifying docs/LEGAL.md — French co-ownership law obligations and coverage tracking._

# Legal Docs Rules

Source of truth: `docs/LEGAL.md`. Scope: French co-ownership law, RGPD, legal accounting, syndic obligations.

## When to modify

Only when a law/decree/jurisprudence changes, or coverage status changes after an **actual delivery**.

## Mandatory

- New or modified legal obligation → add to `docs/LEGAL.md` **before** any backlog item or ADR.
- Every legal reference must cite the official text: Légifrance LEGIARTI ID + version + effective date.
- Never interpret the law — quote official texts verbatim.
- Coverage gap (⚠️ partial / ❌ uncovered) → must point to an explicit Epic or story in `docs/EPICS.md`.
- ✅ coverage → only after actual delivery, never after planning.
- Never delete an obligation — archive with "repealed by [text] on [date]" if necessary.
- No external references (ADR, ticket numbers) in `docs/LEGAL.md` body — refs only.

## Do not put here

Technical implementation → `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` + ADR. Product workflows → `docs/PRD.md`. UX → `docs/DESIGN.md`.

## Rule: doc-prd

_Rules for modifying docs/PRD.md and docs/product/PRD - *.md feature files._

# PRD Docs Rules

Source of truth: `docs/PRD.md` (master) + `docs/product/PRD - {feature}.md` (per-feature detail).

## When to modify

`docs/PRD.md`: only to add/remove a feature, update product vision, or fix transversal info (roles, legal constraints, architecture summary). Feature detail lives in its own PRD file.

## Mandatory

- `docs/PRD.md` body contains no external technical references (ADR, DDR, ticket numbers).
- Abandoned features → send to **Cimetière** section with justification. Never delete.
- Before starting any work: check if request matches an existing PRD or Epic. If yes → confirm before proceeding.
- Feature PRDs with legal constraints must reference `docs/LEGAL.md`.
- Link functional decisions to technical constraints via ADR/DDR refs — in feature PRDs, not in `docs/PRD.md`.
- No external references (ADR, DDR, ticket numbers) in `docs/PRD.md` or `docs/product/**/*.md` body — refs only.

## Do not put here

Technical implementation → `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Design/components → `docs/DESIGN.md`. Legal text → `docs/LEGAL.md`.

## Rule: foundational-docs-sync

_Foundational docs (ARCHITECTURE, DESIGN, EPICS, PRD) must be updated in the same change as the code that invalidates them._

# Foundational document sync

The four foundational docs are contracts, not archives:

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — technical architecture and module descriptions.
- `docs/DESIGN.md` — product identity and design system.
- `docs/EPICS.md` — epic/story backlog and delivery status.
- `docs/PRD.md` — product vision, users, features, constraints.

## Rules

- Any change that invalidates a foundational doc (new table/module/route,
  new design component, story delivered, feature scope change) updates the
  doc **in the same commit**, not in a follow-up.
- Story delivery updates its status in `docs/EPICS.md`; a new design-system
  component updates `docs/DESIGN.md`; a schema change updates
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- Structural changes only: keep these docs free of implementation detail;
  detail belongs in `docs/specs/`, ADRs and DDRs.
- Never delete an invariant from a foundational doc without verifying it is
  no longer enforced in code.
- If a change is too large for in-place update, flag the doc with a dated
  "outdated" note and open an issue — never leave silent drift.

## Rule: licensing

_Licensing rules: dual AGPL-3.0 / commercial license, AGPL-compatible dependencies, zero telemetry, mandatory CLA._

# License & compliance

- The project is under a **dual license**: AGPL-3.0 for non-commercial use, a commercial license for commercial use (see `LICENSE`, `docs/LEGAL.md`).
- Any new dependency (Rust or npm) must be **AGPL-3.0 compatible**; check the license before adding to the manifest, and update `NOTICE` if required.
- **Zero telemetry**: no usage data collection, no tracking dependency, no non-functional outbound network call.
- Any external contribution goes through the CLA (`CLA.md`).
- Never introduce code whose license imposes obligations incompatible with the dual license.

## Rule: pull-request-template

_Pull requests must follow .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and Conventional Commits._

# Pull request conventions

- Every PR must be filled in following `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (all its sections, in order).
- Title follows Conventional Commits (`type(scope): summary`), same as every commit in the branch.
- PRs target `main`; never commit directly to `main`.
- The description must list: what changed, why, doc impact (foundational docs updated or untouched with justification), and testing evidence.
- If the PR changes schema, API contracts, or the design system, link the corresponding ADR/DDR and doc sections.
